title: Burst credits reinitialized on worker restart causing quota overshoot
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Symptoms: several high-throughput customers reported quota overruns where per-key/per-org burst allowances appeared to be applied twice during short maintenance windows. Observed behavior: when a rate-limiter worker process restarts (OOM, deploy, or scaling event), traffic routed to a different worker briefly consumed burst credits that were subsequently reinitialized locally and then reconciled with Redis, resulting in effective double-crediting for a subset of requests. Impact: measurable revenue leakage and incorrect throttling behavior for affected tenants; blurred SLO behavior for token-bucket enforcements across routes.
root_cause_summary: The rate limiter maintains a hybrid model: authoritative counters in Redis and a local in-memory burst-credit cache for latency-sensitive checks. On worker restart, missing or delayed checkpoint reconciliation causes the local cache to default to the "initial burst value", and subsequent reconciliation logic merges the local default with the authoritative counter using a non-atomic read-modify-write path. Race conditions between reconciling workers and inflight requests create windows where credits are double-counted. Additionally, the current reconciliation path does not use a Redis Lua script or CAS semantics, so concurrent reconcilers can both write increments.
repro_steps: 1) Configure an org/route with small steady-state rate and non-zero burst credits. 2) Drive sustained traffic to exhaust steady tokens and rely on bursts. 3) Kill the current rate-limiter worker (SIGKILL) during a window with in-flight requests. 4) Allow another worker to continue serving while the restarted worker performs state reconciliation. 5) Observe that requests served during reconciliation consume 'refilled' burst credits leading to overshoot. 6) Capture metrics: increment counts, Redis writes, and request traces from both workers.
metrics_observed: - Billing meter drift: ~2-5% increased billed tokens for affected routes during incidents (from Grafana: panel rate-limiter.billing-drift, spike around 2026-02-27)
temp_mitigation: - Immediate: reduced worker restart concurrency by staggering deploys and disabling aggressive autoscaling for high-throughput pools. - Short-term patch: add a feature flag to force authoritative Redis checks on first request after restart (fall back adds ~5-10ms p99). Deployed behind flag to runtime-1.21 for top 10 tenants.
proposed_fixes: 1) Replace the non-atomic reconciliation with a single Redis Lua script that calculates proper delta and applies CAS-style semantics. 2) Add a leader-election (single-writer) lease per org-route so only one reconciling worker can initialize credits at a time. 3) Persist local cache checkpoints more frequently and use monotonic version tags to prevent applying stale defaults. 4) Add integration tests that simulate concurrent reconcilers and verify no double-crediting. 5) Instrument a reconciliation audit log to detect future anomalies.
tradeoffs_decision_notes: - Lua script approach: atomic and minimal runtime latency but increases complexity of Redis scripts and coordination for shard changes. - Leader lease: simpler correctness model but introduces availability coupling; if leader cannot acquire lease, requests fall back to authoritative check adding latency. Decision: implement Lua script in short-term for correctness (runtime-1.22) and follow up with leader-lease pattern if we see performance regressions.
